subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
passage:
“Imran! Imran, hold my jacket!”

“I can't reach you! Someone said the gate is closing!”

“Who said that?” Uday's voice shook. “Nobody said that, they just shouted!”

“Keep your arms up, chest clear,” a steward called from the wall. “Don't run. Walk with them.”

A girl screamed behind him and the whole line lurched. Uday's feet left the ground for a second. “I can't breathe properly, I can't...”

“Uday, look at me! Step left, toward the light!”

Another surge. Then a gap opened by the barrier, and the steward's hand shot out and pulled Uday sideways. Imran arrived a moment later, white-faced.

“It was a rumour,” Imran gasped. “The gate never closed.”

Uday sat on the kerb, shaking. “I was so angry at those people. Then I realised they were as scared as me.”

qa.q: What did someone say about the gate?
qa.a: Someone said the gate is closing.

qa.q: What did Uday mean by saying the crowd was as scared as Uday?
qa.a: Uday first felt angry at the pushing crowd, then understood that everyone was frightened and moving out of panic.

qa.q: What did the steward do that helped Uday get out of the crush?
qa.a: The steward called out to keep arms up and walk with the crowd, and then pulled Uday sideways through a gap by the barrier.

qa.q: What was it like for Imran, unable to reach Uday in the crush?
qa.a: Imran was probably terrified and helpless, shouting across the crowd, and arrived white-faced once Uday was pulled free.

grounding: A person in a dense concert crowd is pushed by a panicking mass, where fear and a false rumour spread faster than information.

passage:
I'm Neelam, and I still dream about the footbridge at the riverside fair. After the fireworks everyone left at once, and the bridge was narrow. Nandini and I held hands. Then somebody at the front shouted that the rail had broken. It hadn't, but nobody knew that. The crowd leaned, and I felt my ribs squeezed by strangers' backs. I couldn't move my arms. I wanted to scream, but my breath wasn't there.

What I remember most is that nobody was cruel. People were just afraid, all at once, and fear travelled faster than any fact. Nandini pulled me sideways into a gap by the pillar. A volunteer called, “Slowly, slowly, keep going.” We reached the road and sat on the kerb, shaking, holding hands hard.

qa.q: Who did Neelam hold hands with on the bridge?
qa.a: Neelam and Nandini held hands on the bridge.

qa.q: Why did the crowd lean when somebody shouted that the rail had broken?
qa.a: People were afraid, and fear travelled faster than any fact, since nobody knew the rail was fine.

qa.q: What choice helped Neelam get out of the crush?
qa.a: Nandini pulled Neelam sideways into a gap by the pillar, and they kept going slowly as the volunteer called.

qa.q: What might the volunteer have been trying to do by calling, “Slowly, slowly, keep going”?
qa.a: The volunteer was probably trying to keep the mass moving steadily so nobody fell, while hoping to calm the crowd.

grounding: A person on a narrow bridge is pushed by a panicking mass, where fear spreads faster than information and the danger is the crowd's movement.
